title: WTJU 91.1: The Charlottesville Frequency
author: Claudette
description: The UVA college radio station (mid-late 1980s) that seeded Silver Jews, Pavement, Yo La Tengo's classic lineup, and Jagjaguwar/Secretly Group — plus the Ectoslavia/Red House scene and the Songs: Ohia bridge

nodes.name: Darius Van Arman
nodes.note: music director → dropped out for a label

essay:
Every one of these threads eventually runs back to a single room: the DJ booth at WTJU 91.1, the free-form, student-run college radio station at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, in the mid-to-late 1980s.

The cast: David Berman (Col '89, English/poetry) had a 2-6 a.m. shift he described later as 'The music was the education. WTJU was the study hall.' Stephen Malkmus (Col '88, history), a year ahead of Berman, was another overnight DJ, and met Berman and Bob Nastanovich through the station and the Charlottesville show circuit. James McNew, a Charlottesville native studying Japanese at UVA, was DJing there too. And Darius Van Arman, a few years behind them, became WTJU's music director before dropping out to found a record label out of overtime pay.

Out of that scene came Ectoslavia, Berman's chaotic noise-collage project based in the 'Red House' group house. Malkmus and Nastanovich were both kicked out of it by Berman. After graduation, Malkmus and Berman both moved to New York and took jobs as security guards at the Whitney Museum. In 1989 they started recording home tapes as Silver Jews — the same year Malkmus's other project, Pavement, put out its debut EP. McNew joined Yo La Tengo as permanent bassist in 1992. Van Arman started Jagjaguwar in 1996; three years later it merged with Secretly Canadian to form Secretly Group.

None of these bands ever really 'belonged' to Charlottesville in the public imagination — Berman used to joke he was preparing for a future where more people said 'David Berman was from here' than said it about Dave Matthews. That hasn't happened. But the tape collection at a college radio station clearly did something.
